difficulty_reason: In the situation of the taut descent statements of the chapter, the lemma asserts that if the target ring is pre-admissible then so is the source (statement lines 1838-1843). The proof follows the same scheme as the neighbouring descent statements: it fixes a weak ideal of definition of the target and an open ideal of the source whose extension lies inside it, and reduces the assertion to showing that the closure of a power of that open ideal lies inside an arbitrary open ideal of the source (proof lines 1845-1849). For an arbitrary open ideal it takes the closure of its extension in the target and uses injectivity of the faithfully flat map between the quotients to reduce to a containment inside that closure, which holds for large powers because the extension of the chosen ideal is contained in a weak ideal of definition of the target and the closure is open (proof lines 1849-1854). The claim is H2: the reduction and the descent of the containment are both displayed, and the argument is a genuine transfer rather than a citation.
